subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this durable runtime as a core, user-configurable shared-state and recovery subsystem across agent front doors, or keep durability improvements within existing owner-specific lifecycle paths?
rationale: This is a permanent product and architecture choice: it adds root config, persisted state, startup/fallback behavior, and cross-owner recovery semantics that cannot be safely accepted from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped core design
options.body: Approve a documented durable-core boundary, owner, upgrade contract, and stack order, then invite a narrowly rebased implementation series.

options.title: Keep owner-specific durability
options.body: Decline the new generic core runtime and pursue targeted reliability fixes in existing task, session, subagent, and Gateway owners.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Close this implementation proposal for now and reopen a focused design discussion when durable recovery becomes a current roadmap priority.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped core design
recommendation.body: Approve a documented durable-core boundary, owner, upgrade contract, and stack order, then invite a narrowly rebased implementation series.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only concrete routing candidate supplied for the full proposed stack; final product ownership needs an actual maintainer sponsor.
